subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 4-month-old girl is admitted with persistent oral candidiasis, failure to thrive, and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. She has no palpable lymph nodes or tonsils, and a chest radiograph shows an absent thymic shadow. Laboratory studies show lymphopenia with markedly decreased T cells and poor antibody responses; serum uric acid is normal, and erythrocyte adenosine deaminase activity is undetectable. Her parents are first cousins.
question: Which of the following is the most likely underlying defect?
explanation_correct: Adenosine deaminase deficiency is an autosomal recessive cause of severe combined immunodeficiency and accounts for a substantial minority of cases. Lack of ADA causes deoxyadenosine and dATP to accumulate, and dATP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, depriving lymphocytes of DNA precursors; treatment options include enzyme replacement, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and gene therapy.

explanation_incorrect.A: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase deficiency causes a combined immunodeficiency with prominent T-cell defects and low uric acid, but it does not produce the classic ADA-deficient SCID picture with an absent thymus.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase deficiency causes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome with hyperuricemia and self-mutilation, not severe combined immunodeficiency.
explanation_incorrect.C: Xanthine oxidase deficiency causes xanthinuria with radiolucent kidney stones and has no effect on immune function.
explanation_incorrect.E: PRPP synthetase superactivity causes early-onset gout and hyperuricemia, not thymic aplasia or opportunistic infection.

educationalObjective: Severe combined immunodeficiency with an absent thymus and undetectable adenosine deaminase activity indicates ADA deficiency, an autosomal recessive form of SCID.
